Table 7: Roles of the three contextual variables in our framework. S defines the long-horizon relevance policy, I provides short-horizon behavioral control, and K stores reusable precedents and evidence for cross-agent coordination.

Figure 1: Case-driven multi-agent framework for e-commerce search relevance. The User Agent discovers highvalue bad cases through conversational interaction; the Annotator Agent produces standard-grounded labels under evolving standards S (and optional directives I , more in Appendix C.1); and the Optimizer Agent diagnoses failures and triggers data-centric repairs and retraining. An Automated Iteration Pipeline closes the loop by continuously sampling traffic, updating supervision, and deploying validated model updates, while Global Memory synchronizes standards and case status across agents.

Figure 10: An example of the multi-agent conversational system. The User Agent and the Annotator (Expert) Agent discuss a difficult case with a human, invoke tool-augmented modules to resolve the case, and distill the outcome into Global Memory.
